title: We have a suite of tools that lets AI agents analyze, refine and update games on their own
author: Playgama
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
We’ve been working on a way to give AI game-building agents feedback from actual players. Now we have all necessary tools for making it happen.  
  
Here’s how it works: you build a browser game with an agent, publish it directly from Claude Code or Codex, and get it in front of players through Playgama Sandbox. The agent can then pull gameplay analytics, look for where players drop off, change the game, and upload a new version.

For example, if players keep leaving during the tutorial, the agent can use event data to investigate and update that part of the game. The next batch of player data helps you see whether the change worked.

The tools behind this are Playgama MCP, Sandbox, and Bridge SDK. The idea is to make it easier to keep developing a game after the first playable build.

If you’ve built a game with AI, what happened after your first version?   
Did you get people to play it, and how did you decide what to improve?
